newsitem.title: USA: Echo Bay to omit dividends to fund mines.
newsitem.headline: Echo Bay to omit dividends to fund mines.

text.p: Echo Bay Mines Ltd on Tuesday said it would suspend common stock dividends to fund development of two new gold mines -- Aquarius in Canada and Paredones Amarillos in Mexico.
The company also said it would take a $77 million after-tax charge, equal to $0.55 per share, to write off the Alaska-Juneau property in Alaska as of December 31.
The decision, approved by Echo Bay's directors, to proceed with the mines is contingent on arranging financing.
The Paredones decision is also contingent on Viceroy Resource Corp, a 40 percent owner, approving the project and obtaining its share of financing.
Echo Bay currently produces about 725,000 to 750,000 ounces of gold a year from four mines in the United States and Canada.
The two new mines will together produce about 240,000 to 250,000 ounces a year for Echo Bay's account, it said.
The target for starting up the mines is late 1998, with full-scale commercial production expected by early 1999. Paredones Amarillos will be the largest gold mine in Mexico.
Total production costs of the two new mines are expected to average about $320 to $325 per ounce, including depreciation, amortization and reclamation, Echo Bay said.

The new mines will add 2.0 million ounces of gold to Echo Bay's proven and probable reserves as of the end of 1996. Alaska- Juneau's reserves of 3.4 million ounces and other mineralization of 1.6 million ounces will be removed from Echo Bay's total gold resources as of December 31, it said.
Echo Bay will have to invest $167 million during the next two years to bring the two new mines into production.

Cash operating costs for the gold produced at the two new mines are expected to average about $220-225 per ounce, compared with Echo Bay's current consolidated cash operating costs of $245-$255 per ounce, it said.

The company said it intended to finance Aquarius with a new $75 million unsecured corporate credit facility. Paredones Amarillos is to be financed with a $36 million non-recourse project loan, subject to arrangement of satisfactory terms. Most of the remaining funds will come from cash on hand and operating cash flow from Echo Bay's four existing gold mines.

Echo Bay said the divdend suspension would save about $21 million during the next two years for mine development, based on the companmy's prior practice of paying a semiannual dividend of US$0.0375 per common share.
Bringing the Alaskan project into production would have required an additional investment of more than $300 million during the next four years, it said.

The company's decision to write off the project results from a fresh feasibility study. It was based on a new mine plan incorporating geological information from a two-year underground drilling program completed in 1995.
